error: A detail contradicts the passage.
shows: Cannot locate evidence.
example: "Mira waits by the sink" beside "Ada waits by the art-room sink."
if_many: Reread the answering line aloud with a finger, then replace the detail. 5 minutes, next day's opening repair.

error: A trait replaces the response to an event.
shows: Does not link an event to an action.
example: "Leo is shy" beside "He asks Mira to push the window with him."
if_many: Lay the event card beside two action cards; the child picks the action that answers it. 5 minutes, next day's opening repair.

error: An image is named without its contribution.
shows: Names what is pictured but not what it clarifies.
example: "The crate is brown" beside "Each girl holds one handle, so they carry it together."
if_many: Cover the words and ask what the picture shows; then say it with "The picture shows ___ so Mira ___." 5 minutes, next day's opening repair.

error: The writing has no explanatory topic.
shows: Facts are not tied to a point.
example: "Books are nice" beside "Reading partners work together."
if_many: Name what the piece explains before adding facts. 5 minutes, writing conference.

error: A fact or word meaning is unsupported by its source.
shows: Cannot trace a fact to a sentence.
example: "Partners read on Fridays in the gym" beside "Pupils read with partners each Tuesday after lunch."
if_many: Trace each fact to a source sentence and replace it if it is not there. 5 minutes, writing conference.

error: A needed word is left undefined.
shows: Uses a word without its meaning.
example: "Reading partners read together" with no meaning of partner beside "A partner is someone who works with another person."
if_many: Add its meaning from the source beside its first use. 5 minutes, writing conference.

error: The writing has no conclusion.
shows: Stops without an ending that follows the facts.
example: "A partner works with another person." beside "Working together helps them read."
if_many: Add an ending that follows the facts. 5 minutes, writing conference.

error: A speaker interrupts another turn.
shows: Does not wait for the signal.
example: Talking over a partner beside waiting for the two-finger signal.
if_many: Rehearse the wait signal once with the class. 3 minutes inside the day's talk part.

error: A comment is unrelated to the previous remark.
shows: Does not link to the last idea.
example: "My bag is green." beside "You said Leo waited. His waiting let you finish."
if_many: Say the last speaker's idea first, then add: "You said ___; I would add ___." 3 minutes inside the talk part.

error: An unclear explanation is accepted without clarification.
shows: Says OK instead of asking.
example: "OK" to "They moved it over there" beside "Which detail do you mean?"
if_many: Ask "Which part do you mean?" and wait. 3 minutes inside the talk part.

error: A question ignores what the speaker said.
shows: Asks about something else.
example: "What is your favourite food?" beside "You said together. How do they share the task?"
if_many: Say back the speaker's idea, then ask about it. 3 minutes inside the talk part.

error: Long and short vowels receive the same sound.
shows: Reads kit and kite, or hop and hope, alike.
example: "Kit" and "kite" given one sound beside short i and long i.
if_many: Blend the matched pair, hiding the final e then showing it. 5 minutes, next day's foundations opening.

error: A taught vowel team receives the wrong sound.
shows: Reads ai or ay with a short vowel.
example: Pail read with a short a beside the long a of the ai team.
if_many: Map the whole team to its sound before blending. 5 minutes, next foundations opening.

error: Words are read or heard without key meaning.
shows: Cannot recount the main ideas.
example: "It is about bags" beside "Pupils collect questions, the teacher reads one, and partners find its answer."
if_many: Cover the text and tell three ideas in order with first, then, last. 5 minutes, next day's opening repair.

error: Rushing obscures sentence meaning.
shows: Reads through the full stops.
example: A read with no pause at the full stops beside a read that pauses at each one.
if_many: Read it in phrases with the slash marks, partner then child. 5 minutes, group time.

error: A picture substitutes for decoding.
shows: Names a word from the picture, not its letters.
example: Saying "spades" from the picture beside reading "tools" from its letters.
if_many: Cover the picture, read the letters first, then check against the picture. 5 minutes, foundations opening.

error: A learned spelling pattern is not transferred.
shows: Spells by sound and drops the team.
example: "Pal" for pail beside "pail" with the ai team.
if_many: Compare the new word with its spelling family on the wall. 5 minutes, foundations opening.

error: Spelling is copied without the reference.
shows: Does not consult the entry.
example: Copying "seat" from a partner beside finding seat in the dictionary and comparing the letters.
if_many: Locate the entry, compare the letters and correct the draft. 5 minutes, reference group.

error: The opening and ending functions are confused.
shows: Reread opening and ending together to trace the completed action.
example: "The finished label starts the story" (the day 34 exit and the day 36 exit) beside "The opening gives Idris his job; the ending finishes it."
if_many: Lay the beginning card and the ending card on the story map and read each aloud with a finger. 5 minutes, next day's opening repair.

error: A detail contradicts the text.
shows: Replace it with the detail in its answering sentence.
example: "Others studied first" (the day 35 exit) or a bubble that asks a different question (the day 33 exit) beside the card's order and its own question.
if_many: Retell the card with three picture strips in order; the child places each strip. 5 minutes, next day's opening repair.

error: One paragraph detail is named as the whole topic.
shows: Compare all paragraph focuses before naming what joins them.
example: "The topic is shells" for a text about shell shapes and tracks (the day 46 exit) beside "The topic is clues about past life."
if_many: Read the title and the first lines, name the topic, then check each paragraph fits it. 5 minutes, day 47 opening repair.

error: An author purpose is unsupported by the text.
shows: Point to what the author actually explains or describes.
example: "The author wants to sell pencils" (the day 48 exit) beside the sentence that says what the author explains.
if_many: Ask "What does the author say in the first line?" and cover the invented purpose. 5 minutes, day 49 opening repair.

error: A useful text feature is ignored during a search.
shows: Choose the feature that leads directly to the requested fact.
example: A child searches every part instead of using a subheading (the day 47 exit) or takes the label route for tracks (the day 49 exit).
if_many: Show the question beside the route cards and walk the finger from subheading to bold word to caption. 5 minutes, next day's opening repair.

error: A mold is confused with a cast.
shows: Match the hollow and the filled shape to their captioned names.
example: "A mold is what fills the hollow" beside "A mold is the hollow shape the shell left" (page 8). First met day 36; matters for day 57.
if_many: Draw the shell, the mud and the hollow in three boxes and label the mold. 5 minutes, day 37 opening repair; do not use cast.

error: An irrelevant word meaning is chosen.
shows: Test each meaning in the actual sentence.
example: "Fan is something that blows air" beside "fan-shaped mark".
if_many: Say the word in its sentence, then reject the meaning that does not fit the sentence. 5 minutes, day 38 opening repair.

error: The prefix meaning is mistaken.
shows: Join the known prefix meaning to the known base meaning.
example: "Unfinished means finished again" (the day 50 exit) beside "un- means not".
if_many: Flip the word card: finished / unfinished; say not finished. 5 minutes, day 51 opening repair.

error: The known root meaning is lost.
shows: Connect the new word to its root in the sentence.
example: "Careful means not caring" or "recorder erases" beside "careful is full of care".
if_many: Cover the ending, say the small word, then add the ending's meaning. 5 minutes, day 38 opening repair.

error: Compound parts are joined with a meaning that does not fit.
shows: Combine the parts, then check the result in context.
example: A compound whose parts are joined but do not fit (the day 51 exit: "a book made of grass") beside "a book of outdoor notes".
if_many: Predict, then read the sentence and check that the meaning fits; if not, try the other sense of a part. 5 minutes, day 52 opening repair.

error: The narrative has no elaborated event.
shows: Expand one moment rather than listing unrelated facts.
example: An event with one sentence and nothing more beside an event with action, thought and feeling.
if_many: Add one detail card to the first sentence. 5 minutes, day 46 opening repair.

error: The narrative gives no character action.
shows: Add what the character does in that event.
example: A paragraph of feelings with no action beside "I leaned close."
if_many: Ask "What did you do?" and add one action. 5 minutes, day 46 opening repair.

error: The narrative gives no character thought.
shows: Add what the invented character wonders or thinks.
example: No thought in the event beside "I wondered what it was."
if_many: Hold up a thought bubble; the child finishes "I wondered ___". 5 minutes, day 46 opening repair.

error: The narrative gives no character feeling.
shows: Add a feeling tied to the event.
example: No feeling beside "I felt puzzled."
if_many: Use the feeling word chart and pick one that fits. 5 minutes, day 46 opening repair.

error: The narrative has no time words.
shows: Add temporal words to show event order.
example: A narrative with the events and no order words ("Jo found a shell. Jo drew it.") beside "First Jo found a shell. Then Jo drew it."
if_many: Add First, Then and At last to a strip of three events. 5 minutes, day 34 opening repair.

error: The narrative has no closure.
shows: Finish the event opened at the beginning.
example: An ending that just stops beside "At last Jo knew what it was."
if_many: Reread the story's last page aloud and give the child the closing line to copy. 5 minutes, day 34 opening repair.

error: A collective noun is replaced by a plural noun.
shows: Name the people as one group.
example: "The dogs ran down the hill" where a group word was asked for, beside "A pack of dogs." Day 54 (the day 54 exit).
if_many: Hold the pack card against a single-dog card; say "one group word, many dogs". 5 minutes, day 55 opening repair.

error: An irregular plural is regularized.
shows: Rehearse the singular and irregular plural pair in context.
example: "Two mouses" beside "two mice"; "childs" beside "children". Day 54 (the day 54 exit).
if_many: Flip each plural card: the whole word changes, so add no -s. 5 minutes, day 55 opening repair.

error: A reflexive pronoun mismatches its referent.
shows: Match the pronoun to the person acting.
example: "Bea told himself" or herself read as a second girl (the day 55 exit) beside "Bea told herself".
if_many: Draw one arrow from the actor back to herself; read it aloud with the name. 5 minutes, day 56 opening repair.

error: An irregular past verb is regularized.
shows: Rehearse the present and past pair in context.
example: "Sitted", "hided" or "telled" beside "sat", "hid" and "told".
if_many: Sort today and yesterday cards; read the yesterday card, then say it in a sentence. 5 minutes, day 56 opening repair.

error: An adjective modifies an action in place of an adverb.
shows: Ask whether the description modifies the thing or the action.
example: "She speaks calm" beside "She speaks calmly". Day 56 (the day 56 exit).
if_many: Ask "Is it about a girl or about speaking?"; point to the person card or the action card. 5 minutes, in day 58's Return and repair, since day 57 has no repair slot.

error: A revision loses the narrative focus.
shows: Keep changes connected to the chosen event.
example: A revision that adds a sentence about a picnic (the day 64 exit), beside "It had a curved line."
if_many: Read the feedback aloud; ask "Does this new sentence answer it?"; cross out the one that does not. 5 minutes, day 65 opening repair.

error: Rushing obscures sentence meaning.
shows: Reread in phrases for a listener.
example: A child reading "Was it part of the shell" without a pause or a rising voice (the day 44 exit).
if_many: Model one line twice, racing then pausing; the child copies the pause and the question voice. 5 minutes, day 45 opening repair.

error: A word that fits the meaning is guessed instead of decoding its letters.
shows: Read the letters before checking meaning.
example: "Cart" for "card" or "farm" for "form" because it fits the picture.
if_many: Cover the picture, map each letter, blend, then check the meaning. 5 minutes, next foundations opening.

error: A taught vowel correspondence is misread.
shows: Map the spelling to its taught sound before blending.
example: "Bern" for barn, "shurt" for short, or reading "bird" as "bored".
if_many: Hold the three /er/ spellings (er, ir, ur) beside ar and or on the word wall and blend a matched pair. 5 minutes, next foundations opening.

error: A suffix is omitted in reading.
shows: Blend the base and its ending as one complete word.
example: "Jump" for "jumped" or "turn" for "turns".
if_many: Underline the ending, read it alone, then the whole word. 5 minutes, next foundations opening.

error: A mapped irregular word is regularized.
shows: Remap its unexpected letters and reread the word.
example: "Sayed" for "said" or "yelow" for "yellow".
if_many: Map the unexpected part of the word with a star and write it from memory twice. 5 minutes, next foundations opening.

error: Doubling is omitted before a vowel suffix.
shows: Compare the short-vowel base with its suffixed form.
example: "Runing" for running or "hoping" for "hopping".
if_many: Compare hop and hope: one short vowel and one consonant, so double. 5 minutes, next foundations opening.

error: A spelling is copied without consulting its reference.
shows: Locate the entry and compare its letters with the draft.
example: A child spells "orange" without looking at the word wall after being told to check.
if_many: Model the check: say the word, find it on the wall or in the beginning dictionary, copy it, cover, write. 5 minutes, next foundations opening.

error: A sentence is incomplete.
shows: Add the missing subject or predicate before expanding it.
example: "Because it blocks the wind." as the whole answer (day 41 written answers) beside "She needs the box because it blocks the wind."
if_many: Say the whole sentence aloud first, then write it with a capital and an end mark. 5 minutes, day 42 opening.

error: A proper name is left lowercase.
shows: Capitalize each word in the particular name.
example: "earth day", "lake huron", "wes" in lowercase (the day 65 exit and the day 66 exit), beside "Earth Day", "Lake Huron", "Wes".
if_many: Hold up a common-name card and a special-name card; ask "Is it one special holiday, place or product?" 5 minutes, day 66 or 67 opening repair.

error: A letter greeting or closing lacks its comma.
shows: Place the comma after the greeting or closing.
example: "Dear Wes" or "See you soon" with no comma.
if_many: Walk a finger down the model letter and stop at each comma. 5 minutes, day 67 opening repair.

error: A possessive apostrophe is omitted.
shows: Mark who owns the named thing with the apostrophe.
example: "Finns tray" beside "Finn's tray".
if_many: Ask "Does the tray belong to someone?" and add the mark. 5 minutes, day 68 foundations opening, since day 68 has no topic repair slot.

error: A contraction apostrophe is omitted.
shows: Mark the missing letters where the words join.
example: "Hed" or "Id" for he'd and I'd.
if_many: Show the apostrophe as the two missing letters in would. 5 minutes, day 58 foundations opening.

error: A child observes publishing without contributing.
shows: Offer a choice of wording or placement to discuss with a partner.
example: A child watches the typed piece without offering a choice.
if_many: Offer a two-choice card in the retry; the child picks and says why. 3 minutes in the day 74 sharing block.

error: An imagined response is attributed to a historical person without evidence.
shows: Separate the source's stated facts from the invented narrator's response.
example: "Mary felt happy when she found the skeleton" (the day 43 exit) beside "The account says she found it; a reader may imagine a feeling and say so."
if_many: Cover the thought bubble, read the fact card aloud, then ask who has the idea. 5 minutes, day 44 opening repair.

error: Seed dispersal is mistaken for pollination.
shows: Pollination and seed dispersal are not told apart.
example: "Because the wind carries the kernels" beside "Because pollen landed on the silk."
if_many: Day 84: match pollen between flowers to its caption. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: Steps are listed without connections.
shows: The facts are known but not how one leads to the next.
example: "Sam sets out water. A sparrow drinks" beside "Sam sets out water, so the sparrow can drink. (Or: The sparrow drinks because Sam set out water.)"
if_many: On 84 or 118, explain one arrow using because before adding the next. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: A fact contradicts its source.
shows: A claim is not checked against its source.
example: "The sparrow drinks, so Sam sets out water" beside "Sam sets out water, so the sparrow can drink. (Or: The sparrow drinks because Sam set out water.)"
if_many: Day 103: replace it with the answering sentence's fact. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: Copying replaces shared participation.
shows: The child has not yet added a part of their own to the shared work.
example: "A bean seed sleeps in a dry jar. When it gets wet, it swells" beside "Water (card 1), or water and warmth (the picture), in a few words."
if_many: Day 103: contribute one located fact to the joint question. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: A fact does not answer the research question.
shows: Relevance to the question is not yet judged.
example: "a seed sleeps in a jar" beside "Water (card 1), or water and warmth (the picture), in a few words."
if_many: Day 103: match each fact to the question. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: The paragraph has no introduced topic.
shows: The child does not yet say what the paragraph is about.
example: "Points to the first sentence" beside "The finger is on A bill is a bird's beak."
if_many: Day 103: add a sentence naming what it explains. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: The paragraph has no conclusion.
shows: The child does not yet know how to close an explanation.
example: "It is one more fact" beside "It ends the paragraph by saying why the bird helps the flower."
if_many: Day 103: add an ending that completes the explanation. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: The paragraph has no definition.
shows: The child does not yet explain a topic word for a reader.
example: "Points to a fact; no word is explained" beside "The definition sentence."
if_many: Day 103: explain one necessary topic word. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: Copying replaces content revision.
shows: Feedback has not yet changed the ideas in the draft.
example: "Copies the same draft out again" beside "A new sentence that answers the feedback question."
if_many: Day 103: change one unclear idea using written feedback. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: A spelling is copied without consulting a reference.
shows: A reference is not yet used to check a spelling.
example: "Looks at a neighbor and copies the spelling" beside "The child finds the entry, compares the letters and writes cattle."
if_many: Day 103: locate the entry before comparing letters. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: The speaker interrupts.
shows: Waiting for a turn is not yet a habit.
example: "Talks over the speaker" beside "Waits and listens, then speaks."
if_many: Day 103: rehearse gaining the floor with a turn card. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: The response does not link to the previous remark.
shows: The child does not yet build on what was said.
example: "I like drawing" beside "Any question the next card could answer, such as Where does the pollen stick?"
if_many: Day 103: name the idea being extended. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: The listener asks no clarifying question.
shows: The child does not yet ask when something is unclear.
example: "Says nothing, or says a fact" beside "Any question the next card could answer, such as Where does the pollen stick?"
if_many: Day 103: ask about an unclear detail. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: The answer ignores the speaker's words.
shows: The question asked is not heard.
example: "Beetles are big" beside "An answer the card gives, such as On its back."
if_many: Day 103: restate the speaker's question before answering. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: A requested sentence is a fragment.
shows: A full sentence is not yet the habit when detail is requested.
example: "Because pollen on the leg" beside "The pollen sticks to the visitor and rubs off on the next flower."
if_many: Day 116: supply its missing subject or predicate. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: A word is repeated without a real-life connection.
shows: The word is known by sound but not by use.
example: "Bumpy is bumpy" beside "A real place or thing with bumps, such as a stony road or an orange peel."
if_many: Day 116: name a real situation the word describes. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: Closely related words are treated as identical.
shows: The difference in strength or size is not yet heard.
example: "Shows the same speed for both" beside "The dash: a slow walk shown, then a quick run shown."
if_many: Day 116: contrast their meanings in the poem. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: An adjective modifies an action.
shows: Describing words for actions and for things are not yet sorted.
example: "A slowly slug" beside "A word that describes the slug, such as slimy, small or gray."
if_many: Day 116: name the action before choosing its adverb. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: A picture supplies a guess instead of decoding.
shows: The picture is used instead of the letters.
example: "Reads pumpkin as melon" beside "Reads the four sentences with every word right, or right after one prompt."
if_many: In the next teaching group, blend from printed letters.

error: A taught vowel correspondence is misread.
shows: A taught vowel sound is not yet secure.
example: "Cub" beside "Cube."
if_many: In the next teaching group, remap that vowel before blending.

error: A live telling replaces an audio recording.
shows: No audio record has been made.
example: "Tells the story live; no recording is saved" beside "A saved audio recording of the story exists and plays."
if_many: On 116 for rehearsal or 118 for newly collected evidence, save actual audio during rehearsal. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: The drawing does not clarify the recorded story.
shows: The drawing does not yet help a listener.
example: "A drawing of a house that is not in the story" beside "The drawing shows the action or feeling the story tells."
if_many: On 116 for rehearsal or 118 for newly collected evidence, draw the scene described in the recording. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: The child watches publication without contributing.
shows: The child has not yet taken a part in the shared product.
example: "I watched my partner do it" beside "A named choice the child took part in making."
if_many: On 116 for rehearsal or 118 for newly collected evidence, choose wording or placement with a partner. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: A home variety is ranked as inferior English.
shows: A home way of speaking is treated as wrong.
example: "Here is what happened is bad English" beside "I shall describe the visit."
if_many: Before 118, contrast purpose and listener relationship without ranking varieties. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: The taught final spelling is omitted.
shows: The taught ending is not yet applied to a new word.
example: "fidle" beside "The word fiddle, spelled with every taught letter and in order."
if_many: In the next teaching group, compare the base pattern with the new word.

error: The story gives no descriptive detail.
shows: Events are told without detail a listener can picture.
example: "A story with events but no descriptive detail" beside "A connected flower visit with facts, descriptive detail and a clear voice."
if_many: On 116 for rehearsal or 118 for newly collected evidence, add a detail that helps a listener picture the event. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: The story cannot be heard.
shows: The voice does not yet carry to the recorder.
example: "A story told too softly to hear" beside "A connected flower visit with facts, descriptive detail and a clear voice."
if_many: On 116 for rehearsal or 118 for newly collected evidence, rehearse an audible phrase at the recording distance. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: A useful text feature is ignored.
shows: The text features that locate a fact are not yet used.
example: "I just know it" beside "Word parts: un- and curl."
if_many: Day 84: choose the heading that leads directly to the requested fact. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: One paragraph focus is substituted for the whole topic.
shows: The focus of one paragraph is mistaken for the whole topic.
example: "It is about nectar" beside "How pollination helps later plants and later visitors."
if_many: Day 84: compare the paragraph focuses before naming what joins them. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: Adult-selected facts replace independent gathering.
shows: The answers were found by an adult, not by the child.
example: "The one my teacher told me to write" beside "A fact the child chose from the card, not one the adult handed over."
if_many: Day 103: provide the source pages without highlighting the answer. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: A fact is attributed to the wrong source.
shows: Notes are not yet traced to the source that gave them.
example: "The picture card." beside "The text card (the fact is in the text)."
if_many: Day 103: trace the note back to its answering sentence. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: The definition's explanatory role is not recognized.
shows: The job of a definition in an explanation is not yet seen.
example: "Points to A long, thin bill reaches nectar deep inside a flower" beside "The finger is on A bill is a bird's beak."
if_many: Day 103: connect the defined word to the fact it helps explain. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: The written story gives no narrated action.
shows: The written story has no event for the character to do.
example: "I am a bee. Flowers" beside "Words that tell an action, such as landed or sipped."
if_many: Day 118: add what the character did using written feedback. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: The written story gives no thought.
shows: The written story has no thought to show the character's mind.
example: "Flowers. Nectar" beside "Words that tell a thought, such as wondered."
if_many: Day 118: add an imagined thought linked to its event. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: The written story gives no feeling.
shows: The written story has no feeling.
example: "The bee flew" beside "Words that tell a feeling, such as excited."
if_many: Day 118: add a feeling linked to its event. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: Temporal words do not signal written event order.
shows: Time words are not yet used to order events.
example: "A flower. A leaf" beside "Time words, such as first, next and at last."
if_many: Day 118: choose a time word joining two events. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: The written story gives no closure.
shows: The written story does not yet end.
example: "Pollen. Pollen" beside "A last sentence that ends the visit, such as At last I flew home."
if_many: Day 118: add an ending that completes its event. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: An affix is treated as meaningless.
shows: The meaning an affix adds is not yet used.
example: "Uncurls means curls" beside "Un- undoes curl, so the tongue unrolls."
if_many: In the next teaching group, connect the affix to its change in meaning.

error: An irregular word is read as if it were spelled regularly.
shows: The odd part of an irregular word is not yet noticed.
example: "Reads head with a long e" beside "The word head rhymes with bed."
if_many: In the next teaching group, mark the odd part of the word, then read it.

error: Letters of a taught ending are written out of order.
shows: The order of the letters of a taught ending is not yet secure.
example: "nibbel" beside "The word nibble, spelled with every taught letter and in order."
if_many: In the next teaching group, say the ending's letters in order, then write them.

error: A vowel-team spelling is swapped for another with the same sound.
shows: Which vowel-team spelling a word needs is not yet secure.
example: "jau" beside "The word jaw, spelled with every taught letter and in order."
if_many: In the next teaching group, compare the word's meaning and the heard sound with the team it needs.

error: A meaning is given that the words do not support.
shows: A meaning is given without checking it against the words.
example: "Stored means thrown out" beside "Put away safely."
if_many: Day 116: point to the words that support the meaning. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: Events are recounted out of order.
shows: The order of the events is not yet secure.
example: "Rain, gathering, building" beside "Gathering, building, rain."
if_many: Day 120: lay the three cards, say first, next, last aloud, and tell the story with finger pointing. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: The moral has no support in events.
shows: A lesson is stated without an event that holds it up.
example: "The lesson is: do not sing" beside "Get ready before a hard time, because the ants gathered grain."
if_many: Day 121: ask the pair which event shows the lesson, then put a dot on it. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: Different characters are given identical viewpoints.
shows: What each character wants is not yet told apart.
example: "Mouse thinks the cave is safe" beside "Mouse thinks the cave is not safe."
if_many: Day 125: read each animal's line and say what that animal wants before voicing it. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: A comparison omits a difference.
shows: A detail found in only one version is not yet found.
example: "Both have an ant" given as the difference beside "She asks to borrow."
if_many: Day 122: hold the two request lines side by side and point to the words only one has. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: A comparison omits a similarity.
shows: An event both versions share is not yet found.
example: "They are not alike" beside "The grasshopper sings in both."
if_many: Day 123: find one thing that happens in both on the side-by-side print. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: A minor detail replaces an important point.
shows: The point the paragraph's details support is not yet named.
example: "Wash the dish each week" beside "Birds need a dish of water."
if_many: Day 135: name the point the paragraph's details support. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: A reason is attached to the wrong point.
shows: Which point a reason explains is not yet checked.
example: "A bright jacket is warm" beside "Drivers can see bright colours from far away."
if_many: Day 133: draw an arrow from the reason to the point it explains. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: The writing never introduces its topic.
shows: The subject is not yet named in the writing.
example: "I like the garden." beside "Our garden can include native plants and night-blooming flowers."
if_many: Day 136: add a sentence that names the subject. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: The writing states no opinion.
shows: Facts are written and no position is taken.
example: "The floor is slippery." beside "Our school should put up a walking sign."
if_many: Day 136: add the writer's position. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: A reason is irrelevant to the opinion.
shows: The reason is not yet checked against the opinion.
example: "I like herbs." beside "The herbs stay green, so a cook can still pick them."
if_many: Day 137: replace it with a fact from the source that supports the position. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: Reasons lack linking words.
shows: A reason is set beside an opinion with nothing joining them.
example: "Put up a sign. The floor is slippery." beside "Put up a sign because the floor is slippery."
if_many: Day 136: choose a link that joins the reason to the opinion. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: The piece has no conclusion.
shows: The writing stops without finishing the position.
example: A draft that stops after the last reason beside "So let us include both in our garden."
if_many: Day 142: add an ending that completes the position. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: Copying replaces content revision.
shows: The meaning is not yet changed after feedback.
example: The same draft copied neatly beside a draft with the missing reason added.
if_many: Day 142: change one unclear idea using the written feedback. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: A flagged convention is left unedited.
shows: A marked convention is not yet corrected.
example: The marked name left in small letters beside the name with a capital.
if_many: Day 142: correct that convention in a separate editing pass. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: A sound device is named without its effect.
shows: What a sound pattern adds is not yet said.
example: "It repeats" beside "The repeated line keeps the beat and shows the hopping again and again."
if_many: Day 127: connect the sound to the rhythm or the meaning it makes. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: A requested sentence is a fragment.
shows: A whole sentence is not yet the habit when detail is asked for.
example: "The reeds." beside "Heron asks because the reeds need the water."
if_many: Day 157: supply the missing subject or verb. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: A first letter or word shape supplies a guess.
shows: The word is guessed, not blended from every letter.
example: "city" read as "cat" beside "city" blended letter by letter.
if_many: Day 120: cover the picture, touch each tile and blend. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: A taught spelling pattern is not transferred.
shows: The pattern taught is not yet used in a new word.
example: "cityes" beside "cities."
if_many: Day 120: ask whether the letter before the y is a consonant or a vowel, then write the word. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: A spelling is not checked with a reference.
shows: The printed beginning dictionary is not yet used to check a spelling.
example: "partys" left as written beside "parties" found in the entry.
if_many: Day 122: find the entry word, then say what changed. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: A comment ignores the previous remark.
shows: The idea just said is not yet picked up.
example: "I like blue." after "The ant worked hard" beside "I agree the ant worked hard."
if_many: Observed, not scored. In the next talk part, name the idea being extended. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: The child interrupts a speaker.
shows: Waiting for a turn is not yet secure.
example: Speaking over a partner beside waiting for the turn card.
if_many: Observed, not scored. In the next talk part, rehearse gaining the floor with a turn card. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: The listener leaves confusion unexplained.
shows: A confusing phrase is not yet asked about.
example: Nodding at "borrow" beside "What does borrow mean?"
if_many: Observed, not scored. In the next talk part, ask about one unclear phrase. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: An answer ignores the speaker's question.
shows: The question is not yet kept in mind while answering.
example: "I like the grasshopper" in answer to "What does the ant say?" beside "The ant says she is storing food."
if_many: Observed, not scored. In the next talk part, restate the question before answering. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: Closely related words are treated as identical.
shows: The small differences between close words are not yet heard.
example: "Toss" used for "place" beside "place the seed gently."
if_many: Day 144: order place, drop and toss by motion, and small, tiny and minute by size in printed contexts. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: An adverb is used to describe a noun.
shows: What a word describes is not yet checked before choosing its form.
example: "a gentle water" beside "water gently."
if_many: Day 144: identify what the word modifies before choosing its form. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: Planting steps have no explained connection.
shows: Why one step must come before the next is not yet said.
example: "Add soil. Add seed." beside "Add soil first, because the seed needs a place to rest."
if_many: Day 146: explain why one step must precede the next. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: Watching publication replaces contributing.
shows: Making one wording or placement choice is not yet happening.
example: Watching a partner type beside choosing a word and saying why.
if_many: Day 148: make and explain one wording or placement choice. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: The oral-reading answer contradicts the passage.
shows: The answer does not match what the passage says.
example: "May gives the berries to the babies" beside "It holds her own snack."
if_many: Day 123: reread the sentence that answers the question. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: Oral phrasing obscures sentence meaning.
shows: Pauses are not yet placed where the meaning needs them.
example: Reading across a full stop beside pausing at each sentence end.
if_many: Day 123: mark the phrase boundaries and reread for meaning. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: A misread word remains unconfirmed after checking.
shows: The letters and the sentence are not yet used to confirm a word.
example: Keeping the puppet's word beside matching every letter and testing the meaning.
if_many: Day 123: match every letter, test the meaning and reread the sentence. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: A printed word is read incorrectly.
shows: The sounds are not yet mapped to the letters of the whole word.
example: "berries" read for "babies" beside "babies" mapped sound by sound.
if_many: Day 123: map its sounds to its letters and read the whole word. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: A required sound device is left out of a poem explanation.
shows: One of the devices is not yet found and explained.
example: Talk about rhyme alone beside beat, rhyme, alliteration and repetition each with its effect.
if_many: Day 151: add the missing device and say what it adds to rhythm and meaning. 5 minutes, next teaching day's opening repair.

error: A word is guessed from its first letter or shape, not read from its letters.
shows: Decoding is replaced by guessing.
example: Says mud for mat beside: m, a, t blended
if_many: Cover the first letter; touch each letter, say its sound, then blend. 5 minutes, a reteach group on the response day.

error: A passage is read word by word, with no phrasing and no end marks.
shows: The reading does not sound like talking.
example: Reads each word at one pitch beside: reading in phrases
if_many: Echo one line, then read it together, the voice dropping at the full stop. 5 minutes, a reteach group on the response day.

error: A misread is left: the reader goes on after a sentence stops making sense.
shows: Sense is not checked against the words.
example: Reads cashes for catches and goes on beside: rereads and fixes the word
if_many: Read a line with one planted wrong word; stop at the end and ask whether it made sense. 5 minutes, a reteach group on the response day.

error: A vowel pattern is read with the wrong sound, or part of the word is dropped.
shows: A pattern is not applied.
example: Says spin for spine beside: spine
if_many: Sort word cards by pattern and say each word by its pattern. 5 minutes, a reteach group on the response day.

error: An ending is dropped or changed when the word is read.
shows: The ending is not read.
example: Says mop for mopped beside: mopped
if_many: Build the word with tiles: the base first, then the ending. 5 minutes, a reteach group on the response day.

error: A pattern that does not always sound the same is read by its usual sound.
shows: The second sound is not tried.
example: Says breed for bread beside: bread
if_many: Say the usual sound, then the other, and keep the one that makes a word. 5 minutes, a reteach group on the response day.

error: An unusual word is sounded out letter by letter or read as another word.
shows: The unusual part is not marked.
example: Says sho-e for shoe beside: shoe
if_many: Map the word: star the part that does not do what its letters usually do. 5 minutes, a reteach group on the response day.

error: A spelling stops at the sound and misses the pattern.
shows: A pattern is not transferred to a new word.
example: Writes prays for praise beside: praise
if_many: Sort word cards by pattern, then build a new word with tiles. 5 minutes, a reteach group on the response day.

error: A wrong spelling is left, or a right word is changed.
shows: The dictionary is not used to check.
example: Writes cold for colt beside: meadow, cheek
if_many: A guide-word hunt: find a word on the page and say how you knew where it was. 5 minutes, a reteach group on the response day.

error: A question has no question word, or the text does not answer it.
shows: A text question is not composed.
example: Do you like art? beside: Who helped Cora?
if_many: Point to a line in the text and turn it into a question that starts who, what, where, when, why or how. 5 minutes, a reteach group on the response day.

error: An answer comes from the child own life or ideas, not the text.
shows: Evidence is not used.
example: Because it is cold beside: because the path is wet
if_many: Put a finger on the line that says it and read it back. 5 minutes, a reteach group on the response day.

error: An answer fits a different question word.
shows: The question word is not heard.
example: To go home for when beside: at three
if_many: Say each question word with the kind of answer it wants: who a person, where a place, when a time. 5 minutes, a reteach group on the response day.

error: A trait stands for what a character does.
shows: No response to an event is given.
example: Cora is a nice girl beside: she asks the helper for oil
if_many: Ask what happened, then what the character did about it. 5 minutes, a reteach group on the response day.

error: A recount gives one thing, or a thing the text does not say.
shows: Key ideas are not recounted from what was heard.
example: Wear boots and bring a toy beside: pack lunch and wear boots
if_many: Say the message back in two parts, one thing it asks for each finger. 5 minutes, a reteach group on the response day.

error: The narrative has a setting but no actions, thoughts or feelings.
shows: The event is not elaborated.
example: The lights went out. It was dark. beside: I held my desk and felt scared
if_many: Add one thing you did and one thing you felt to a plain sentence. 5 minutes, a reteach group on the response day.

error: The narrative has no time words, or the events run together.
shows: The order is not signalled.
example: and the teacher came and we sat beside: first, then, at last
if_many: Number the events, then add a time word to each. 5 minutes, a reteach group on the response day.

error: The narrative has no ending.
shows: No sense of closure is given.
example: First the lights went out. Then we waited. beside: at last the lights came back
if_many: Ask how it ended and write that last. 5 minutes, a reteach group on the response day.

error: The text is read, but its topic is not said.
shows: One detail or nothing stands for the topic.
example: The floor is dry beside: a boot spot keeps the floor dry
if_many: Ask what all the sentences are about, then what one sentence adds. 5 minutes, a reteach group on the response day.

error: A liking stands for what the reader will find out or gets.
shows: Purpose is not stated.
example: I like boots beside: what a boot spot is
if_many: Use the frame: I read this to find out ___. 5 minutes, a reteach group on the response day.

error: A detail from the text is named, but not the one asked.
shows: The question is not matched to the line.
example: To come inside beside: it is time for lunch
if_many: Reread the question, then find the line with its words in it. 5 minutes, a reteach group on the response day.

error: An opinion sentence has no link word, or the wrong fact as its reason.
shows: The reason is not joined to the opinion.
example: We should keep a jar. It saves a walk. beside: because it saves a walk
if_many: Choose the fact that helps, then add because. 5 minutes, a reteach group on the response day.

error: A comparison names one card only, or no likeness or difference.
shows: Two texts are not set side by side.
example: Beans need water beside: both need sun, but one grows in a bed
if_many: Lay the cards side by side and finish: Both ___, but ___. 5 minutes, a reteach group on the response day.

error: A prefix is dropped, or read as part of another word.
shows: The prefix is not separated.
example: Says unfar for unfair beside: un and fair
if_many: Put the prefix on a flap over the base word and read each, then the whole. 5 minutes, a reteach group on the response day.
